example_2: Do you happen to know where she is?
example_3: I happened to see him yesterday.

phrase_en: As far as I’m concerned, the matter is closed.
phrase_sk: Pokiaľ ide o mňa, tá vec je uzavretá.
example_2: As far as I'm concerned, you can stay.
example_3: As far as I know, he's still in London.

phrase_en: We might as well stay here until the rain stops.
phrase_sk: Môžeme tu rovno zostať, kým neprestane pršať.
example_2: We might as well start now.
example_3: You might as well tell the truth.

phrase_en: He’s on the verge of a nervous breakdown.
phrase_sk: Je na pokraji nervového zrútenia.
example_2: They are on the verge of signing the contract.
example_3: The species is on the verge of extinction.

phrase_en: I’m not in the mood for going out tonight.
phrase_sk: Nemám náladu na to, aby som išiel večer von.
example_1: To be in the mood for [noun/ing].
example_2: Are you in the mood for a movie?
example_3: I'm not in the mood to talk right now.

phrase_en: Suppose you won the lottery, what would you do?
phrase_sk: Predpokladajme, že by si vyhral lotériu, čo by si robil?
example_2: Suppose he doesn't show up?
example_3: Suppose we went by train instead?

phrase_en: I’ve been tied up with work all day.
phrase_sk: Celý deň som bol zavalený prácou.
example_2: I'm tied up at the moment.
example_3: She's tied up in a meeting.

phrase_en: It’s unlikely that they will agree to our terms.
phrase_sk: Je nepravdepodobné, že pristúpia na naše podmienky.
example_2: It's unlikely to happen.
example_3: Is it unlikely that she will come?

phrase_en: I’ve run out of patience with them.
phrase_sk: Došla mi s nimi trpezlivosť.
example_2: We've run out of milk.
example_3: I'm running out of time.

phrase_en: In spite of the weather, we went for a walk.
phrase_sk: Napriek počasiu sme išli na prechádzku.
example_2: In spite of being tired, she worked late.
example_3: He failed in spite of his efforts.

phrase_en: It never occurred to me that he was lying.
phrase_sk: Nikdy mi nenapadlo, že klame.
example_2: Did it occur to you to ask him?
example_3: It occurred to me that I forgot my keys.

phrase_en: I can’t make head or tail of this document.
phrase_sk: Neviem z tohto dokumentu vyjsť (nerozumiem mu).
example_1: Can't make head or tail of [something].
example_2: I can't make head or tail of his handwriting.
example_3: We couldn't make head or tail of the map.

phrase_en: There’s no point in arguing with him.
phrase_sk: Nemá zmysel sa s ním hádať.
example_2: What's the point of waiting?
example_3: There was no point in staying longer.

phrase_en: I’ll get around to fixing it eventually.
phrase_sk: Nakoniec sa dostanem k tomu, aby som to opravil.
example_2: I haven't got around to reading that book yet.
example_3: When will you get around to doing your homework?

phrase_en: How come you didn’t tell me before?
phrase_sk: Ako to, že si mi to nepovedal predtým?
example_2: How come you're so late?
example_3: How come they didn't invite us?

phrase_en: Judging by his face, he’s not happy.
phrase_sk: Súdiac podľa jeho tváre, nie je šťastný.
example_2: Judging by the sky, it's going to rain.
example_3: Judging by her accent, she's from Australia.

phrase_en: I’m under the impression that we’ve met before.
phrase_sk: Mám dojem, že sme sa už stretli.
example_1: To be under the impression that...
example_2: He was under the impression that the meeting was canceled.
example_3: I was under the impression you knew.

phrase_en: It stands to reason that they will be late.
phrase_sk: Je logické (dáva to zmysel), že budú meškať.
example_2: It stands to reason that prices will rise.
example_3: It stands to reason that if you don't study, you won't pass.

phrase_en: I’ve put off doing my taxes for too long.
phrase_sk: Príliš dlho som odkladal podávanie daní.
example_2: Don't put off until tomorrow what you can do today.
example_3: They put off the wedding until next year.

phrase_en: He takes after his father in many ways.
phrase_sk: V mnohých ohľadoch sa podobá na svojho otca.
example_2: Does she take after her mother?
example_3: He takes after his grandfather.

phrase_en: I can’t put my finger on what’s wrong.
phrase_sk: Neviem presne pomenovať (ukázať), čo je zle.
example_2: Something is different, but I can't put my finger on it.
example_3: I couldn't put my finger on the reason for my anxiety.

phrase_en: It’s hard to keep track of all the changes.
phrase_sk: Je ťažké sledovať (mať prehľad o) všetky tie zmeny.
example_2: How do you keep track of your expenses?
example_3: I've lost track of time.

phrase_en: I’d like to point out that we are over budget.
phrase_sk: Rád by som poukázal na to, že sme nad rozpočtom.
example_2: She pointed out a mistake in the report.
example_3: I must point out that time is running out.

phrase_en: He’s been going through a lot lately.
phrase_sk: V poslednom čase si toho veľa prešiel (zažil zlé veci).
example_2: She went through a difficult divorce.
example_3: We are going through some changes at work.

phrase_en: You can count on me whenever you need help.
phrase_sk: Môžeš so mnou rátať kedykoľvek budeš potrebovať pomoc.
example_2: I'm counting on your support.
example_3: Can I count on you to be there?

phrase_en: What if we tried a different approach?
phrase_sk: Čo keby sme skúsili iný prístup?
example_2: What if it rains?
example_3: What if we don't succeed?

phrase_en: He’s been looking into the possibility of moving.
phrase_sk: Skúmal možnosť sťahovania.
example_2: The company is looking into new markets.
example_3: We are looking into ways to reduce costs.

phrase_en: I’ve been struggling to keep up with the workload.
phrase_sk: Mám problém stíhať to pracovné zaťaženie.
example_2: It's hard to keep up with technology.
example_3: Slow down, I can't keep up with you.

phrase_en: I’ve come to the conclusion that we need a change.
phrase_sk: Dospel som k záveru, že potrebujeme zmenu.
example_1: To come to the conclusion that...
example_2: What conclusion did you come to?
example_3: I've come to the conclusion that he's right.

phrase_en: He ended up working for a rival company.
phrase_sk: Skončilo to tak, že pracoval pre konkurenčnú firmu.
example_2: We got lost and ended up in a small village.
example_3: How did you end up here?

phrase_en: It’s up to you to decide what to do next.
phrase_sk: Je na tebe, aby si sa rozhodol, čo robiť ďalej.
example_2: The choice is up to you.
example_3: It's not up to me to judge.

phrase_en: I didn’t mean to hurt your feelings.
phrase_sk: Nechcel som zraniť tvoje city.
example_2: I didn't mean to wake you up.
example_3: He didn't mean to be rude.

phrase_en: I wish I had known about this earlier.
phrase_sk: Kiežby som o tom vedel skôr.
example_2: I wish I had more time.
example_3: I wish I hadn't said that.

phrase_en: He tends to exaggerate his achievements.
phrase_sk: Má tendenciu zveličovať svoje úspechy.
example_2: Prices tend to rise in summer.
example_3: I tend to get nervous before exams.

phrase_en: I can’t believe how much things have changed.
phrase_sk: Nemôžem uveriť tomu, ako veľmi sa veci zmenili.
example_2: I can't believe he's only twenty.
example_3: I can't believe it's already Friday.

phrase_en: He was taken aback by her reaction.
phrase_sk: Bol zaskočený jej reakciou.
example_2: I was taken aback by the news.
example_3: She was taken aback by his rudeness.

phrase_en: I’ve been putting a lot of thought into this.
phrase_sk: Veľa som nad tým premýšľal.
example_2: You clearly put a lot of thought into this gift.
example_3: We need to put more thought into the plan.

phrase_en: Is there any chance of getting a discount?
phrase_sk: Existuje nejaká šanca na získanie zľavy?
example_2: Is there any chance of rain?
example_3: Is there any chance that he will come?

phrase_en: I’m not sure if I can make it to the party.
phrase_sk: Nie som si istý, či stihnem prísť na párty.
example_2: Did you make it to the meeting on time?
example_3: I'm sorry, I can't make it tonight.

phrase_en: It’s a matter of time before they find out.
phrase_sk: Je to otázka času, kým na to prídu.
example_1: It’s a matter of time before...
example_2: It's only a matter of time.
example_3: It's a matter of life and death.

phrase_en: I’m not very good at small talk.
phrase_sk: Nie som veľmi dobrý v nezáväznej konverzácii.
example_2: He's good at solving problems.
example_3: She's not very good at keeping secrets.

phrase_en: He’s been looking for a way out of the situation.
phrase_sk: Hľadal spôsob, ako sa z tej situácie dostať.
example_2: There's no way out.
example_3: We need to find a way out of this mess.

phrase_en: I’m not in a position to give you advice.
phrase_sk: Nie som v pozícii, aby som ti dával rady.
example_1: To be in a position to [verb].
example_2: I'm not in a position to help you right now.
example_3: Are you in a position to sign the contract?

phrase_en: It goes without saying that we will help.
phrase_sk: Netreba ani hovoriť (je to samozrejmé), že pomôžeme.
example_2: It goes without saying that you're invited.
example_3: It goes without saying that safety comes first.

phrase_en: I’ve been trying to get hold of you all morning.
phrase_sk: Celé ráno som sa ťa snažil zastihnúť.
example_2: Where can I get hold of a copy?
example_3: I finally got hold of him yesterday.

phrase_en: How do you go about finding a new job?
phrase_sk: Ako postupuješ pri hľadaní novej práce?
example_2: How should I go about applying?
example_3: He went about his business as usual.

phrase_en: I’m looking forward to seeing how it turns out.
phrase_sk: Teším sa na to, ako to dopadne.
example_2: It turned out better than expected.
example_3: As it turned out, he was right.

phrase_en: I’ve been trying to keep a low profile lately.
phrase_sk: V poslednom čase som sa snažil byť nenápadný.
example_2: He's keeping a low profile until the scandal blows over.
example_3: I prefer to keep a low profile at work.

phrase_en: It’s a long shot, but it might work.
phrase_sk: Je to málo pravdepodobné, ale mohlo by to fungovať.
example_2: Winning the lottery is a long shot.
example_3: It's a long shot, but let's try it anyway.

phrase_en: He’s been having second thoughts about the move.
phrase_sk: Mal pochybnosti (prehodnocoval) o tom sťahovaní.
example_2: Are you having second thoughts?
example_3: I'm having second thoughts about buying that car.

phrase_en: I’m not sure what you’re getting at.
phrase_sk: Nie som si istý, kam tým mieriš.
example_2: What are you getting at?
example_3: I don't know what she's getting at.

phrase_en: It’s hard to tell the difference between them.
phrase_sk: Je ťažké rozoznať medzi nimi rozdiel.
example_2: Can you tell the difference?
example_3: It's hard to tell the difference between real and fake.

phrase_en: I’ve been trying to get my point across.
phrase_sk: Snažil som sa objasniť (presadiť) svoj názor.
example_2: It's hard to get your point across in a large meeting.
example_3: He finally got his point across.

phrase_en: How long has this been going on?
phrase_sk: Ako dlho to už trvá?
example_2: What's going on?
example_3: This can't go on any longer.

phrase_en: I’ve been looking for an excuse to visit you.
phrase_sk: Hľadal som zámienku, aby som ťa navštívil.
example_2: I need an excuse to leave.
example_3: He's always looking for an excuse to complain.

phrase_en: It’s high time we did something about it.
phrase_sk: Je najvyšší čas, aby sme s tým niečo urobili.
example_2: It's high time you cleaned your room.
example_3: It's high time the government took action.

phrase_en: I’m not as young as I used to be.
phrase_sk: Už nie som taký mladý, ako som býval.
example_1: Not as [adjective] as [someone] used to be.
example_2: I'm not as fit as I used to be.
example_3: The town isn't as quiet as it used to be.

phrase_en: He’s been trying to get away with it for years.
phrase_sk: Roky sa mu to snažilo prejsť (bez trestu).
example_2: He thought he could get away with murder.
example_3: How did she get away with it?

phrase_en: I’m not sure if I can pull it off.
phrase_sk: Nie som si istý, či to zvládnem (úspešne dokončím).
example_2: It was a difficult task, but they pulled it off.
example_3: Do you think you can pull it off?

phrase_en: It’s only a matter of time before he gives up.
phrase_sk: Je to len otázka času, kým sa vzdá.
example_2: Don't give up!
example_3: He gave up smoking last year.

phrase_en: I’ve been trying to figure out a way to help.
phrase_sk: Snažil som sa prísť na spôsob, ako pomôcť.
example_2: I can't figure out how to use this machine.
example_3: We need to figure out what to do next.

phrase_en: It’s not as easy as it looks.
phrase_sk: Nie je to také jednoduché, ako to vyzerá.
example_2: Cooking isn't as easy as it looks.
example_3: It's not as simple as it seems.

phrase_en: He’s been trying to make up for lost time.
phrase_sk: Snažil sa dohnať stratený čas.
example_2: Nothing can make up for the loss of a loved one.
example_3: I'm trying to make up for my mistake.

phrase_en: I’m not sure what the future holds.
phrase_sk: Nie som si istý, čo prinesie budúcnosť.
example_2: Who knows what the future holds?
example_3: Whatever the future holds, we'll face it together.

phrase_en: He’s been trying to get over his ex-girlfriend.
phrase_sk: Snažil sa preniesť cez svoju bývalú priateľku.
example_2: It took her a long time to get over the flu.
example_3: I can't get over how much he's grown.

phrase_en: I’m not sure if I should go or stay.
phrase_sk: Nie som si istý, či mám ísť alebo zostať.
example_2: I don't know whether to laugh or cry.
example_3: We haven't decided whether to buy it or not.

phrase_en: It’s hard to keep a straight face.
phrase_sk: Je ťažké zachovať vážnu tvár.
example_2: I couldn't keep a straight face when he told the joke.
example_3: It's important to keep a straight face during the interview.

phrase_en: He’s been trying to get his act together.
phrase_sk: Snažil sa dať dokopy (začať sa správať zodpovedne).
example_2: You need to get your act together if you want to keep your job.
example_3: I'm finally getting my act together.

phrase_en: I’m not sure if I can count on him.
phrase_sk: Nie som si istý, či s ním môžem počítať.
example_2: I'm counting on you!
example_3: Can I count on your help?

phrase_en: It’s hard to put into words how I feel.
phrase_sk: Je ťažké vyjadriť slovami, ako sa cítim.
example_2: I can't put into words how grateful I am.
example_3: Some things are hard to put into words.

phrase_en: He’s been trying to get his point across.
phrase_sk: Snažil sa objasniť svoju pointu.
example_2: I'm trying to get my point across.
example_3: Did you get your point across?

phrase_en: I’m not sure if I can make it.
phrase_sk: Nie som si istý, či to zvládnem (stihnem/dokážem).
example_2: I'm sorry, I can't make it.
example_3: We made it just in time!

phrase_en: It’s hard to keep up with the news.
phrase_sk: Je ťažké držať krok so správami.
example_2: I can't keep up with all the changes.
example_3: It's hard to keep up with him.

phrase_en: He’s been trying to get a head start.
phrase_sk: Snažil sa získať náskok.
example_2: We need a head start.
example_3: Giving him a head start was a mistake.

phrase_en: I’m not sure if I can afford it.
phrase_sk: Nie som si istý, či si to môžem dovoliť.
example_2: I can't afford to buy a new car.
example_3: Can you afford it?

phrase_en: It’s hard to get used to the cold weather.
phrase_sk: Je ťažké zvyknúť si na chladné počasie.
example_2: I'm getting used to it.
example_3: Have you got used to your new job yet?

phrase_en: He’s been trying to get rid of his old car.
phrase_sk: Snažil sa zbaviť svojho starého auta.
example_2: I need to get rid of these old clothes.
example_3: How can I get rid of this headache?

phrase_en: I’m not sure if I should tell him.
phrase_sk: Nie som si istý, či mu to mám povedať.
example_2: I'm not sure whether to go.
example_3: I don't know whether to tell her.

phrase_en: It’s hard to keep a secret.
phrase_sk: Je ťažké udržať tajomstvo.
example_2: Can you keep a secret?
example_3: I'm not very good at keeping secrets.

phrase_en: He’s been trying to get in touch with you.
phrase_sk: Snažil sa s tebou spojiť.
example_2: I'll get in touch with you soon.
example_3: How can I get in touch with him?

phrase_en: I’m not sure if I can trust him.
phrase_sk: Nie som si istý, či mu môžem dôverovať.
example_2: I trust you.
example_3: Can I trust him?

phrase_en: It’s hard to believe it’s already over.
phrase_sk: Je ťažké uveriť, že už je po všetkom.
example_2: I can't believe it.
example_3: It's hard to believe he's gone.

phrase_en: He’s been trying to get a promotion.
phrase_sk: Snažil sa o povýšenie.
example_2: I hope I get a promotion.
example_3: She got a promotion last month.

phrase_en: I’m not sure if I can handle it.
phrase_sk: Nie som si istý, či to zvládnem (uniesiem/vyriešim).
example_2: I can handle it.
example_3: Can you handle the pressure?

phrase_en: It’s hard to make a decision.
phrase_sk: Je ťažké urobiť rozhodnutie.
example_2: Have you made a decision yet?
example_3: It's a difficult decision to make.

phrase_en: He’s been trying to get his life back on track.
phrase_sk: Snažil sa vrátiť svoj život do starých koľají.
example_2: We need to get the project back on track.
example_3: Everything is back on track now.

phrase_en: I’m not sure if I should laugh or cry.
phrase_sk: Nie som si istý, či sa mám smiať alebo plakať.
example_2: I don't know whether to laugh or cry.
example_3: It was so funny I didn't know whether to laugh or cry.

phrase_en: It’s hard to keep track of time.
phrase_sk: Je ťažké sledovať čas.
example_2: I've lost track of time.
example_3: How do you keep track of time?

phrase_en: He’s been trying to get his point across.
phrase_sk: Snažil sa objasniť svoju pointu.
example_2: I'm trying to get my point across.
example_3: Did you get your point across?

phrase_en: I’m not sure if I can make it to the meeting.
phrase_sk: Nie som si istý, či stihnem prísť na stretnutie.
example_2: I can't make it.
example_3: Did you make it?

phrase_en: It’s hard to keep up with the demand.
phrase_sk: Je ťažké držať krok s dopytom.
example_2: We can't keep up with the demand.
example_3: It's hard to keep up with him.

phrase_en: He’s been trying to get a refund.
phrase_sk: Snažil sa o vrátenie peňazí.
example_2: Can I get a refund?
example_3: I'd like a refund, please.

phrase_en: I’m not sure if I should accept the offer.
phrase_sk: Nie som si istý, či mám prijať ponuku.
example_2: I'm not sure whether to accept.
example_3: I don't know whether to go.

phrase_en: It’s hard to imagine what it was like.
phrase_sk: Je ťažké si predstaviť, aké to bolo.
example_2: Can you imagine?
example_3: I can't imagine living there.
